## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The `--json` branch takes whatever token comes next as its path, even when that token is another flag, so `--json` doesn't work with `--junit` in the common order. Fix that before merging. I found nothing to report under silent-failure or comments, and no separate test gap beyond what the correctness finding covers.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — With `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])`, the condition `if i + 1 < len(args): destination = args[i + 1]` sets the JSON destination to `"--junit"` and skips that token. The next token, `"out.xml"`, is then read as a flag and raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. The `--junit` branch just above already guards against this with `args[i + 1].startswith("--")`. Could the `--json` branch use the same check (in both line 15 and line 18) so it falls back to `"results.json"` when the next token is a flag? A test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` would cover that path. — The PR says `--json` should work "alongside the required --junit destination", but putting `--json` before `--junit` is rejected. Through `write_reports`, the same input would try to write a file literally named `--junit`.

## Strengths
- `test_required_junit_path` covers all three outcomes of the `--junit` guard: a valid path, a missing path at the end, and a following flag (`["--junit", "--json"]`).
